newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Fernandez promises no policy U-turns.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Fernandez promises no policy U-turns.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said in an interview with La Nacion newspaper published Thursday that there is no turning back on economic policy despite a wave of social protests.
"The government is not going to give any sign of backtracking," said Fernandez.
"The economic path President (Carlos) Menem has taken is the right one. The program generates jobs, possibilities of real growth and takes care of programs for the least privileged."
Opposition parties and the Catholic Church have attacked the government's economic policies in recent weeks in the face of rising social protests in some provinces by the unemployed and the poor.
Protests in the province of Jujuy grabbed the headlines recently after unemployed sugar and steel workers mounted roadblocks, set fire to piles of tires and clashed with the police two weeks ago.

But the minister said, "The government is more worried about guaranteeing the credibility of the (economic) model and a reliable legal system than giving in to blackmail and seeing on television tires being burnt during an electoral year."
Jujuy and other provincial governments blamed central government for failing to provide funds to help their poor and unemployed, but the economy minister refuted such allegations.

"The provinces now have more resources and more responsibilities," he said. "We have fulfilled all our budgetary promises (to the provinces). Nothing is owed to them, we have even accepted their pension deficits."

Fernandez accepted that not all social problems in the country have been resolved. But he said there was no threat to economic policies, "which are being consolidated day by day, and we know that the opposition will try to take electoral advantage of the social issues."
He also voiced his optimism that unemployment, currently above 17 percent, is falling.

"We have certain data that employment is rising in Argentina. We are close to fulfilling our forecast of a two percent drop in the jobless rate this year, and maybe unemployment will fall a point more," said the minister.
